chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about al-qasāmah: whether a sunnah (prophetic precedent) had been established regarding it. He said, then said:

“Yes. Two men from the Anṣār went out, obtaining provisions from Banī al-Najjār. Then they separated, and one of them was found slain. His companions said to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘Only the Jews killed our companion.’ So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘The Jews shall swear an oath.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can you make the Jews swear regarding our brother while they are a disbelieving people?’ He said: ‘Then you swear.’ They said: ‘And how can we swear about what we did not know and did not witness?’ He said: So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله paid his blood-money from his own possession.”

He said: I said, ‘How was al-qasāmah?’ He said, then said: “Indeed, it is true; and were it not for that, people would kill one another. Al-qasāmah is only a protective measure by which the people are safeguarded.”

key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: the legal procedure of oaths used in a homicide case when direct proof is lacking
key_terms.قَتِيلًا: a slain person, one found killed
key_terms.يَحْلِفُ: swears an oath in legal procedure
key_terms.يُحَاطُ: by which protection is given or people are surrounded with safeguarding

ai.seo_question: What is the basis of al-qasāmah in Islamic law, and why was it instituted?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that al-qasāmah has a sunnah-based legal foundation in a case of unexplained killing. It presents a precedent from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and explains that qasāmah serves as a protective judicial measure to preserve people's lives and restrain unlawful killing.
